title: One Bite From This Snake Could Kill 100 People (Nobody Ever Has Died)

scenes.text: One bite from this snake carries enough venom to kill 100 people.
The inland taipan of Australia. The most venomous land snake on Earth.
scenes.keywords: inland taipan snake desert close up

scenes.text: One bite can hold 110 milligrams of venom. One milligram kills a person.
Untreated, you'd typically be dead within 45 minutes. The same dose kills 250,000 mice.
It lives in empty desert and hunts rats, so it rarely meets people.
And the twist: there is no confirmed human death from it. Ever. 100 per bite, and zero.

description:
The inland taipan is the most venomous land snake on Earth: the largest venom yield from a single bite, about 110 milligrams, is enough to kill roughly 100 adults or 250,000 mice.
Without antivenom a bite would typically be fatal within about 45 minutes. Yet because it lives in remote outback Australia and strikes defensively, there is no confirmed human death from an inland taipan on record.

first_comment: Its hatchlings are born with venom nearly as potent as an adult's. Would you rather live near venomous snakes or big cats?
